findings.title: A single NaN in a continuous hue silently collapses the entire color gradient to one color
findings.description: mat2colors' continuous path builds bin edges with np.min/np.max, which propagate NaN; np.digitize against all-NaN edges then maps every finite value to bin 0-clipped ranks, so ALL finite observations get one palette color and the NaN observation gets another. No warning or error is raised. On the default 'hls' palette both endpoint colors are near-identical reds, so a scientist plotting e.g. a behavioral variable with one missing value sees a uniformly-colored plot and may wrongly conclude their variable carries no structure. Control without the NaN produces 20 distinct colors. Matrix hue handles NaN rows separately (silent uniform blend) and categorical hue is unaffected; only the (very common) continuous path is corrupted. Expected: either drop/neutral-color NaN points with a warning, or raise a clear error naming hue and the NaN index.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/jmanning/hypertools')
import numpy as np
from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors
h = np.linspace(0, 1, 20); h[5] = np.nan
cols = mat2colors(h, palette='hls')
print('unique colors with 1 NaN:', len(np.unique(np.round(cols,4), axis=0)))
print('unique colors without NaN:', len(np.unique(np.round(mat2colors(np.linspace(0,1,20)),4), axis=0)))
"
findings.expected: 20 distinct colors for the 19 finite values (or a warning/error about the NaN); the gradient should survive missing values
findings.actual:
unique colors with 1 NaN: 2
unique colors without NaN: 20
(all 19 finite points render as one color [0.86,0.34,0.34], NaN point as [0.86,0.3712,0.34]; hyp.plot(pts, fmt='.', hue=h) renders this silently -- see e6_nan_continuous_hue.png)
docs_impact: hypertools/plot/plot.py (hue docstring should state NaN handling)

findings.title: Categorical hue + line fmt (the default fmt) crashes when the last-seen category has exactly one member
findings.description: reshape_data groups rows by category, then patch_lines appends the NEXT group's first point to every group except the LAST, and interp_array PCHIP-interpolates each group. A final group with a single row reaches scipy's PchipInterpolator with one sample and crashes with 'ValueError: `x` must contain at least 2 elements.' -- a cryptic scipy message that never mentions hue, categories, or the offending group. The crash is ORDER-DEPENDENT: hue=['b']+['a']*19 works (the singleton 'b' group gets patched with a's first point) while hue=['a']*19+['b'] crashes, in both 2D and 3D, with the DEFAULT fmt (a line). Markers-only fmt='.' is fine. Scientists with a rare condition/outlier category hit this instantly.

findings.title: Categorical pandas Series hue with a non-default index crashes with KeyError: 0
findings.description: plot.py:2101 does `hue[0]` to check for tuple entries. On a pandas Series that is LABEL-based indexing, so any categorical Series whose index does not contain the label 0 (e.g. a filtered/sliced DataFrame column, the single most common way scientists store condition labels) raises a bare KeyError: 0 from inside pandas. Numeric Series (any index) work because they take the continuous path before line 2101, and default-index Series work coincidentally -- so the failure appears random to users. The plot() docstring says 'hue : list or numpy array', but DataFrame/Series inputs are accepted everywhere else in hypertools, and three sibling forms already work.

findings.title: Marker+line combo fmt (e.g. 'o-') with continuous/matrix hue silently drops the line and draws a marker at every INTERPOLATED point
findings.description: For combo styles, interpolation is gated on has_line_component() (so 20 points become ~901), but the multicolor rendering branch at plot.py:2674 chooses lines vs markers with the stricter is_line(): 'o-' is not a pure line, so _apply_multicolor_markers scatters ALL ~901 interpolated points and no line artist is drawn at all. Without hue, 'o-' correctly renders a smoothed line PLUS markers at the 20 TRUE sample points (GH #141). With continuous hue the reader instead sees ~45x more 'data points' than exist (dot trails, gaps at speed changes, no connecting line, and the fmt's marker glyph/raw-point emphasis is lost). Contradicts the hue docstring ('combined with a line format this produces multicolored lines whose color varies continuously along each trajectory') and GH #141's combo-style contract.

findings.title: palette given as a list of color STRINGS (hex or named) crashes with a cryptic IndexError on the matrix-hue and colorbar paths
findings.description: colors.py slices palettes with `np.asarray(...)[:, :3]` in mat2colors (line 83, matrix blend) and get_palette_colors (line 142, used by _build_colorbar_info at plot.py:2901 and the plotly backend). A list of hex/named color strings -- the most common way users write custom palettes, and valid for seaborn everywhere -- produces a 1-D string array, so both paths die with 'IndexError: too many indices for array: array is 1-dimensional, but 2 were indexed'. The SAME palette works fine for a plain categorical hue plot (P5b), so support is inconsistent: palette=['#ff0000','#0000ff'] succeeds until the user adds colorbar=True or switches to a matrix hue, then crashes with no mention of palette. Fix is one to_rgb conversion in _get_palette. mat2colors' own docstring says 'palette : str or list -- Seaborn palette name (or list of RGB tuples)'; plot()'s says only 'palette : str' (see -011).
findings.expected: Hex/named-color list palettes accepted uniformly (converted via matplotlib.colors.to_rgb), matching the categorical path and seaborn's own behavior; or a clear error naming palette= and the accepted forms
findings.actual:
matrix: IndexError: too many indices for array: array is 1-dimensional, but 2 were indexed
colorbar: IndexError: too many indices for array: array is 1-dimensional, but 2 were indexed
(tracebacks end at hypertools/plot/colors.py:83 and colors.py:142 via plot.py:2901 _build_colorbar_info)

findings.title: List palettes require >= 100 entries for continuous hue -- undocumented, and the error does not say how to fix it
findings.description: Continuous 1D hue maps through _get_palette(palette, n_bins=100). A custom list palette therefore must supply >= 100 colors or plot() raises 'ValueError: palette supplies 2 colors but 100 are required'. Nothing in the plot() or mat2colors docs mentions the 100-bin requirement for list palettes; the natural user expectation (seaborn-style: a short list defines gradient anchor colors, e.g. sns.blend_palette) is not met, and the message names neither hue nor palette= nor a remedy (use a named palette / supply n_bins colors). Works: categorical hue with a list >= n_categories.

findings.title: colorbar=True with a categorical hue labels ticks 1..n unless legend=True is ALSO passed, though the category names are known
findings.description: The colorbar docstring says discrete tick labels are 'taken from the legend labels/group names (1..n if no names are available)'. findings.title: names= combined with categorical hue: error reports the post-hue GROUP count as the 'dataset' count
findings.description: names= is validated against len(xform) AFTER hue reshapes datasets into category groups. A user passing one name per input dataset (2 datasets) with a 3-category hue gets 'ValueError: names must have one entry per dataset (3); got 2' -- but they passed exactly one name per dataset; the 3 is the hue-group count. Conversely when counts coincide (2 datasets, 2 categories) the names silently label CATEGORY groups, not the datasets the user named (P16 passed with reshuffled semantics). names= and categorical hue are conceptually incompatible; the message (or a dedicated warning) should say hue regrouped the data.

findings.title: None entries in a categorical hue form a fully-salient unnamed color group that consumes a palette slot
findings.description: The hue docstring says 'To label a subset of points categorically, use None entries'. In practice the None points become their own group: they are correctly omitted from the legend, but they render in a fully-saturated palette color drawn from the SAME cycle as the real categories (['a',None,'b'] -> a=red, None=GREEN, b=blue on hls). A reader sees an unexplained salient color, and the named categories' colors shift depending on where None first appears (first-appearance ordering). Expected per the docstring's intent: unlabeled points de-emphasized (e.g. light gray) and palette slots reserved for named categories. Also worth documenting the actual behavior either way.

findings.title: [infra] Stale non-editable hypertools snapshot in .venv site-packages silently shadows the repo for any run not rooted at the repo (audit/dev footgun)
findings.description: INFRA finding (environment, not shipped library code). .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypertools/ contains a REAL (non-editable) 1.0.0.dev0 install dated Jul 9 23:43, while the repo source is newer (colors.py Jul 10 06:46). Python resolves imports by sys.path[0]: scripts executed from any directory OTHER than the repo root import the stale snapshot. Proof: the same mat2colors(np.array([[0.75,0.25]])) call returns the pre-fix collapse-to-argmax color (0.86,0.3712,0.34) via the snapshot and the correct blend (0.73,0.4856,0.47) via the repo source -- i.e. the QC 2026-07 mixture-blend fix is ABSENT from the installed copy, and diff confirms colors.py/plot.py differ. Any test, notebook, or sibling audit unit run from a non-repo cwd is silently validating outdated code. Early results in this audit were affected until detected and re-run with sys.path pinned. Remedy: reinstall editable (pip install -e '.[dev]') or uninstall the snapshot before further release QC.
